messages.cloud.err_404: Not found (404): the model or endpoint does not exist for this provider/key (often a wrong model id or base URL).
messages.cloud.err_408: Timeout (408): the provider took too long to respond. Check your connection and retry.
messages.cloud.err_429: Rate limited (429): too many requests, or over your plan quota. Wait a bit and retry, or check your provider billing/limits.
messages.cloud.err_500: Provider error (500): the provider had an internal error. Usually temporary — retry shortly.
messages.cloud.err_502: Bad gateway (502): the provider is having trouble upstream. Temporary — retry shortly.
messages.cloud.err_503: Service unavailable (503): the provider is down or overloaded. Temporary — retry shortly.

messages.first_run.fact_01: Runs on your machine by default — your prompts never leave it unless you turn on the cloud.
messages.first_run.fact_02: Local chat is free — no per-token meter. Add a cloud key only when you want a bigger model.
messages.first_run.fact_03: No subscription and no per-message fee — it runs on hardware you already own.
messages.first_run.fact_04: Generates images on-device — free, no key, nothing uploaded.
messages.first_run.fact_05: Reads, searches, and edits files in your workspace, and runs tests in a sandbox.
messages.first_run.fact_06: Ask it about a folder and it reads the real files — not a guess.
messages.first_run.fact_07: Bind a chat to a project folder and its memory stays scoped to that project.
messages.first_run.fact_08: Remembers across sessions — everything stored locally on this machine.
messages.first_run.fact_09: Cloud is opt-in: off until you add a key, and you can cap the spend.
messages.first_run.fact_10: Your API keys stay sealed on this machine — encrypted at rest, never shown back.
messages.first_run.fact_11: Switch between local and your own cloud models per chat — you decide, per turn.
messages.first_run.fact_12: Works offline — the local model needs no connection.
messages.first_run.fact_13: A language model just predicts the next word — it looks nothing up unless you hand it a tool.
messages.first_run.fact_14: Models read text as "tokens," not letters — which is why they can miscount the letters in a word.
messages.first_run.fact_15: A "hallucination" is a model stating something false with full confidence — grounding it in real files is the cure.
messages.first_run.fact_16: The "context window" is how much a model can read at once — overflow it and it forgets the start.
messages.first_run.fact_17: "Temperature" tunes randomness: low keeps answers focused, high lets them wander.
messages.first_run.fact_18: Ask a model the same thing twice and you can get two different answers — that randomness is a dial, not a bug.
messages.first_run.fact_19: The same open models behind many cloud assistants can run right here on your desk.
messages.first_run.fact_20: Bigger is not always better — a small local model answers everyday questions instantly.
messages.first_run.opener_1: What are we working on today?

messages.header.model_auto_explainer: Starts local. If the local lane cannot serve a substantive turn and a cloud key is connected, Auto may use the free fallback you choose below. Auto never selects a paid model. Pick any concrete free or paid model to hard-pin that exact model instead.
messages.header.model_connect_note: Connect a provider key in Settings to choose an exact cloud model or configure Auto’s verified-free fallback.
messages.header.model_local_only_explainer: Local Only routes among the models and tools on this machine and never reaches a cloud provider — not paid, not free, not for planning. When a turn needs live or current data, or a model this machine does not have, it says so instead of guessing.
messages.mode.auto_description: Ordinary project reads, edits, tests, and corrections may run autonomously. Destructive, external, publishing, money, credential, and security actions remain protected.
messages.mode.bypass_permissions_description: Highest risk. Requires explicit confirmation, a limited chat or project scope, automatic expiry, and keeps receipts and hard security boundaries active.
messages.mode.manual_description: Answers and safe reads run directly. File edits, commands, network actions, settings, Git, deployment, and messages require an exact approval.
messages.mode.plan_description: Strictly read-only. VOOL can inspect permitted project context and propose a plan; the controller blocks every mutation and side-effecting action.
messages.mode.review_edits_description: VOOL may inspect and prepare edit diffs. Each clearly identified edit batch must be approved before it is applied.

messages.settings.bundle_heading: Export & import a chat portable, signed session bundle
messages.settings.bundle_help: A .voolsession file carries this conversation’s turns, receipts and evidence references, signed by this machine’s key. Encryption is recommended for any bundle leaving this computer; a bundle signed by an unknown key is refused unless you explicitly accept it, and stays marked untrusted. Model-internal reasoning is not part of a bundle. Passphrases exist only in these fields — never in history, logs or receipts.
messages.settings.bundle_plain_warning: I understand an unencrypted bundle can be read by anyone who obtains the file.
messages.settings.cloud_heading: Cloud API key bring your own key
messages.settings.cloud_help: VOOL runs local and free by default. Store a provider key — OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude), Kimi, Groq, Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, or a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint — encrypted on this machine, and test that the provider accepts it. A concrete model you select is a hard pin. OpenRouter :free models cost nothing; paid models spend your provider credits only when you explicitly select one, and remain subject to VOOL’s spend caps. VOOL Auto never selects paid.
messages.settings.key_saved: Key saved and encrypted on this machine.
messages.settings.limits_help: The RAM reserve is enforced live by the resource governor (a bigger reserve means VOOL leaves more for you). The token budget is a guide today, shown against your Usage below — a hard daily cut-off is coming next.
messages.settings.profile_heading: What VOOL remembers about you learned from conversation; yours to change
messages.settings.profile_help: Each item shows its value, scope, origin and last use. Edit, Forget, Move scope and Restore previous act on one item; a candidate from chat waits here until you Save it. Nothing remembered here grants VOOL permission to read, send, post or spend.
messages.settings.report_help: Sanitized draft, exact preview, your approval before anything is sent.
messages.settings.search_heading: Web search key bring your own key
messages.settings.search_help: Paste a search API key — VOOL recognises which service it belongs to and starts using it for live lookups straight away. Keys are stored encrypted on this machine and are never sent anywhere except to that search provider. With no key VOOL keeps using its built-in keyless search; a key simply makes live answers more reliable.
